Writing Suggestions

Understanding the poem and its language

Poetic language (also called poetic devices) are the tools of sound or meaning that a poet can use to make the poem more surprising, vivid, complex, or interesting. Examples of these tools include alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, metaphors similes, and allusion.

Poets don't include poetic language because they want to make their poem sound complicated or hard to understand. Instead, they use these tools to help you wake up, pay attention, and look at the world in new ways.

Activity

Keeping in view the above chart, write a paragraph on the poet use of language in the poem 'The Solitary Reaper' by highlighting various techniques used by the poet.

Oral Communication

Divide the class into two groups. One group may be asked to speak in favour of the rural life and the other to speak in favour of the urban life.

3. What are the poet's feelings about the song as expressed in the second stanza of the poem "The Solitary Reaper"?

4. Describe in your own words the visual images depicted in the first stanza of the poem "The Solitary Reaper".

5. Give the examples of alliteration from " The Solitary Reaper."

6. As you read the third stanza of "The Solitary Reaper" what pictures of the situation do you make in your mind?

7. Explain the last stanza of the poem "The Solitary Reaper" in your own words.

8. What is the dominant theme of the poem The Solitary Reaper"?

Writing Suggestions

Understanding the poem and its language

Poetic language (also called poetic devices) are the tools of sound or meaning that a poet can use to make the poem more surprising, vivid, complex, or interesting. Examples of these tools include alliteration, onomatopoeia, imagery, metaphors similes, and allusion.

Poets don't include poetic language because they want to make their poem sound complicated or hard to understand. Instead, they use these tools to help you wake up, pay attention, and look at the world in new ways.

Use the following chart to record your statement of the meaning of the poem and your observations about the technique of the poem. Each column in the chart deals with one poetic techniques.

Activity

Keeping in view the above chart, write a paragraph on the poet use of language in the poem 'The Solitary Reaper' by highlighting various techniques used by the poet.

Oral Communication

Divide the class into two groups. One group may be asked to speak in favour of the rural life and the other to speak in favour of the urban life.

Vocabulary and Grammar
